To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HSP70 expression is abolished by H. pylori infection, which may lead to apoptosis in gastric epithelial cells, and that the mechanism of HSP70 gene expression abolition is related to the deregulation of heat shock factor 1 and heat shock factor 2.
HSP70 gene expression is abolished in gastric epithelium infected by H. pylori and that this phenomenon is caused by the elimination of HSF1 and the induction of HSF2.

HSP70 gene expression is abolished in the gastric mucosa exposed to H. pylori due to the elimination by H. pylori of the heat shock factors activity, which results in apoptosis of gastric mucosal cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the heat shock protein 70 gene expression abolishment caused by H. pylori infection of the gastric epithelum and the possible involvement of the heat shock factor 1 in this process.
the mechanisms of HSP70 gene expression abolition in gastric epithelium infected with H. pylori.
the elucidation of the mechanism of HSP70 gene expression abolition in gastric epithelium caused by Helicobactor pylori infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism of HSP70 gene transcription inhibition is not related to the induction of apoptosis in the gastric epithelial cells exposed to live H. pylori.
H. pylori ‐induced apoptosis is not a direct consequence of the elimination of HSF1 activity, but it is a consequence of a complex interplay between H. pylori and the host cells.
HSP70 gene expression is abolished due to the lack of heat shock factor 1 and heat shock factor 2 binding to the HSP70 gene promoter in H. pylori‐infected gastric mucosa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
H. pylori‐induced apoptosis is not a consequence of the elimination of HSF1‐mediated HSP70 expression.

the mechanism of HSP70 gene expression abolition in gastric epithelium caused by H. pylori is related to the deregulation of the signal transduction pathway, leading to the inhibition of HSF1 activation and to apoptosis.
the elimination of H. pylori ‐dependent HSP70 gene expression may be a result of a disturbance in the signal transduction pathway, leading to apoptosis of the gastric epithelial cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat shock response is abolished in gastric epithelium infected with H. pylori due to a lack of HSP70 gene expression.
the HSF‐1 and HSF‐3 transcription factors are involved in the transcription of HSP70 gene in the gastric epithelial cells exposed to Helicobacter infection.
HSP70 expression is abolished in the gastric epithelial cell line exposed to H. pylori and that this effect is not mediated by the heat shock response, but rather by the induction of apoptosis.
